newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia plans live sheep trial shipment to Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Australia plans live sheep trial shipment to Saudi.

text.p: A planned trial shipment of live sheep from Australia to Saudi Arabia will open the prospect of a resumption of this once-lucrative trade, Australian meat industry officials told Reuters.
The shipment is expected to take place in a couple of months' time.
Saudi Arabia was Australia's largest market for live sheep, taking more than three million slaughter sheep a year, before it closed its market to Australian imports in 1990.

An Australian Meat and Livestock Corp spokesman said the trial shipment to Saudi, negotiated by Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer during his recent trip to the Middle East, would aim to establish a protocol to re-open exports.

However, AMLC also said in a statement that the Saudi government had confirmed it would close its market to cross-border trade in carcases of slaughtered Australian sheep from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) from May 8 this year.
This was because of Saudi concern about third country processing, AMLC said.
The UAE was by far the largest destination for Australian live sheep exports in 1996, taking nearly 1.8 million head or nearly one-third of total shipments.
It was estimated that up to half of these may be slaughtered for the Saudi carcase trade, AMLC said.

"Unless the Saudi live sheep market can be re-established, and with the ban on the cross-border carcase trade imminent, the outlook for live sheep shipment levels appears less favourable than in the past," it said.

AMLC also said that while Australia's live sheep trade had supported sheep markets in the early part of 1997, live sheep shipments may be constrained during the rest of the year by a shortage of suitable sheep and a decline in shipping capacity.
Tighter capacity was expected after a re-emergence of the live cattle trade to the Middle East caused some sheep carriers on the route to be converted to carry cattle, it said.
Saudi Arabia stopped importing about A$130 million worth of Australian live sheep in 1990 when it rejected several boatloads of animals on health grounds.
In May last year, a ship carrying 75,000 Australian sheep, the first shipment in four years, was diverted to Jordan on fears the animals would fail health tests.

Strict conditions were in place on vaccination against scabby mouth, an AMLC official said. If the trial shipment to Saudi Arabia was successful it would put pressure on the country to re-open the trade, he said.
Australia exported a total of 5.5 million live sheep worth more than A$207 million in 1995/96, most to the Middle East, compared with its total sheep slaughter of 13.9 million.
Australian live sheep exports in January this year of 547,000 head dipped in February to 428,000 head, but buying for March and April shipments had helped support markets, AMLC said.
